policy: Editorial features use only these 250 reviewed public works. New imports enter only after an explicit replacement review. Homepage approval additionally requires a strong initial view, and the live hero requires a preview no larger than 15 MiB.
selection_basis: Curatorial judgment of artistic force, recognizable anchors, visual presentation, material fidelity, documented identity and breadth across regions, periods and makers. Current rendered thumbnails were reviewed; this is not a fresh full-geometry or source-license audit of the entire existing catalog.

The broad seated body, rounded face and layered robe folds remain clear in the carved wood; surviving red, green and gold surface gives the figure a varied, tangible presence.
One leg crosses the other while a hand rises to the cheek, making the pensive pose immediately recognizable; the smooth gilt-bronze body has a strong, open silhouette.
The bronze dancer balances on one leg inside a large flame aureole; extended arms, lifted foot and open gaps make the circular composition readable from a distance.
The terracotta figure folds its limbs tightly around the body, concentrating the pose into a compact mass; the warm, worn surface keeps the sculpture tactile.
A crouching wooden figure supports a broad circular platform above its head; bent knees, large facial features and shell details make the small ritual stand distinctly figurative.
A broad bear face sits beneath a band of inset shell panels; turquoise, red and pale surfaces separate the eyes, mouth and paws across the carved frontlet.

Ganesha's broad belly, long trunk and closely gathered feet form a compact seated mass; the warm andesite surface preserves the depth of the carving.
One raised knee and the leaning torso interrupt the symmetry of the wooden Guanyin; worn red, pale and brown painted areas articulate the relaxed body and drapery.
The vessel spreads into a four-legged animal with an upturned head and curling tail; red-and-cream painting makes the body and small projecting limbs easy to read.
Animal heads, curled projections and dense surface ornament turn the bronze ewer into a compact sculptural creature; the pointed spout and handle remain distinct from the decorated body.
The owl's large round eyes, broad chest and small feet organize a decorated bronze vessel into a clear frontal animal form, with relief patterns visible across the body.
Two large curling horns frame the pale painted ram face; dark openings and repeated ridges give the mask a crisp, immediately readable outline.
The mother's upright body and the smaller child form a closely linked wooden group; the warm reddish surface and applied details distinguish face, torso and surrounding ornaments.
A large face and a bird emerge from the narrow carved panel; white, black and brown pigments separate its interlocking relief forms and shell-set eye.
The helmet retains the swollen fish body, short fins and dense projecting spines; its pale, textured skin makes the unusual material evident before close inspection.
A circular seat and foot ring are joined by open supports covered in small beads; blue, red and pale geometric bands make the stool's structure and surface equally visible.
The seated yogini's bent legs and jar create a substantial, asymmetrical stone form; the broken surrounding arch and worn surface remain clearly distinguishable from the body.
The horse lifts its head above a slender, energetic body; green bronze surfaces and traces of different tones distinguish the mane, legs and broad chest.
Four straight legs and two upright handles frame the rectangular bronze body; dense patterned panels give the vessel a strong architectural outline and worked surface.
The seated figure is dominated by an elaborate headdress, large mask-like face and folded legs; molded ceramic bands and projecting details keep the frontal composition forceful.
The human face rises from a rounded painted vessel beneath a tall headdress and stirrup spout; cream and reddish markings keep the portrait distinct from the container.
The small wooden cat figure combines a large animal head with a tightly gathered upright body; its rounded ears, deep eyes and folded limbs create a memorable silhouette despite the dark surface.
The standing deity fills a deeply carved sandstone surround, with smaller figures and ornament running up both sides; warm surface tones keep the dense relief legible.
The oval treasure box and separate lid display dense carved patterns over dark wood; shell accents and curved edges distinguish the two matching components.
The ivory netsuke concentrates a grinning face into a small oval, with bulging brows, hollow eyes and exposed teeth; dark recesses emphasize the fine carving.
The seated Buddha is framed by a tall halo and a compact carved throne; warm sandstone, folded legs and the raised hands create a clear, balanced frontal composition.
A modeled human face is surrounded by swollen, tapering lobes that spread from the vessel's center; orange and cream slips make the unusual tuber-like body immediately distinct.
A standing figure rises above a painted rectangular base, with a tall curved spout behind it; red and cream surfaces separate the limbs and small narrative details.
A gently curved resting bar bridges low, rounded supports with ribbed wooden surfaces, turning a practical headrest into a compact animal-like composition.
The orange vessel joins two rounded bowls beneath tall curling projections; small painted floral motifs follow the swollen ceramic body.
The standing figure has a long, narrow torso, finely worked headdress and a gently curved stance; the warm stone surface keeps the simplified body distinct from its ornament.
A large face is modeled directly into the red vessel's upright body; the projecting nose, recessed eyes and low foot turn a container into a bold frontal figure.
Ganesha's elephant head rises above a dense seated body, with multiple arms and ornaments spreading to either side; the dark stone surface retains clearly modeled folds and contours.
The upright greenstone figure has a large head, squared shoulders and short, planted legs; its smooth, pale-green body makes the compact human form easy to grasp.
The armored wooden guardian stands above a crouching support figure, with a high staff and lifted arm breaking its outline; surviving color separates the layered costume.
The long wooden body narrows into thin legs beneath a single dramatically raised arm; the stretched silhouette gives the small figure unusual vertical tension.
Large round eyes and a small beak turn the painted jug into a frontal owl; red-brown feather markings remain clear across the pale ceramic body.
The gilt-bronze figure bends gently at the waist and knee, with curling ornaments spreading around the shoulders and hands; its bright surface emphasizes the delicate outline.
Dark inlaid spots and recessed eyes punctuate the ivory leopard face; the oval head, small ears and projecting fangs make the hip ornament distinctly animal-shaped.
A deeply carved face and scrolling headdress dominate the thick limestone fragment; the warm, worn surface keeps the relief readable without presenting it as a complete monument.
The seated wooden Buddha has a broad, calm body and rhythmically carved robe folds; dark brown lacquered surfaces retain the depth of the chest, hands and crossed legs.
Concentric dotted bands spread across the tall oval wooden shield around a projecting center; red, pale and dark pigments make the surface pattern unusually readable.
The ceramic owl has a broad, rounded body, circular facial markings and small projecting feather tufts; its warm brown surface and pale painted rings give it an immediate animal identity.
The seated master's individualized face rises above a heavy robe and compact chair-like base; worn red, pale and dark painted areas distinguish the carved wooden folds.
The broad hat and tiered head make the Gelede mask conspicuous, while cream, black and reddish painted bands emphasize its eyes, cheeks and rounded profile.
A modeled human figure forms the vessel's body beneath a tall stirrup spout; red and cream geometric painting follows the seated torso and separates its facial features.

The rounded fish body is covered with painted scales and sweeping gill lines; a clear tail and small tubular opening preserve the relation between animal and vessel.
The long, low antelope-like headdress balances on short supports; open cuts beneath its body and horns let the warm carved wood form a clear horizontal silhouette.
The seated clay dog has a raised muzzle, broad chest and curled tail; its reddish, textured surface and compact body give the animal a convincing physical presence.
A seated central figure rises among smaller attendants in a dense carved-wood shrine group; projecting limbs and deep gaps make the clustered composition worth turning.
The dark rounded body, bridging spout and small modeled musician form a compact whistling jar; highlights on the smooth earthenware keep the linked parts visible.

Cowrie shells densely edge and stud a rounded textile enclosure; the large circular opening and contrasting blue and red cloth make its layered construction visible.
The tall neck and swollen body are divided by pale geometric bands, with a small modeled face near the shoulders; the pinkish ceramic vessel has a clear vertical profile.
A pale angular face is bracketed by horns and long whisker-like projections, with a spreading bird above it; deep openings make the mask's complex outline readable.
The wooden llama has a long upright neck, short legs and a small opening in its back; the compact orange-brown body makes the ritual container's animal form clear.
A pale face with narrow eyes sits beneath two dark rounded hair masses; strong black-and-white contrast and repeated surface marks make the wooden mask immediately legible.
A small bird head rises from a rounded painted body beneath the bridge and spout; checker-like red-brown and cream markings clearly describe the wings and chest.
Large round eyes outlined with bright metal rings sit inside a red cloth frame; added fabric and shell details extend the carved face into a vivid assemblage.
The duck's raised neck and small head lead into an open bowl-shaped body; pale ceramic and restrained brown painted bands make both animal and container readable.
Four short legs support the rounded buffalo-shaped vessel beneath curling horns and a narrow opening; impressed and painted designs follow the broad earthenware body.
Two small heads emerge from opposite ends of a shared four-legged body; the red ceramic surface and dark markings make the vessel's unusual doubled animal form clear.
Two long, thin bird necks rise above coiling serpent forms at the base; dark red-brown lacquered wood makes the contrast between the airy upper shape and dense lower mass apparent.
Long upright horns and an elongated animal muzzle give the painted wooden Zamble mask a sharp profile; colored bands and recessed eyes break up the dark surface.
Two small human heads terminate a red-brown crescent, turning the long curved pectoral into a balanced sculptural form with expressive ends.
Broad pale cheeks contrast with dark carved hair and a red dividing band; the mask's heart-shaped face and narrow eye slits remain clear within the compact oval.
Rows of shallow incised signs cross a long reddish wooden board; the sculpture-like object rewards close inspection of its carved writing more than a distant silhouette.
Blue floral forms and small red accents ornament the white ceramic jug, while the dark-and-gold mounting and handle outline its rounded body and high neck.
The silver Torah shield joins an architectural relief, a crown and a suspended chain; its gleaming ornament offers a strong example of Jewish ritual metalwork.
Painted floral decoration and a cylindrical wooden case make the Torah scroll’s protective housing a compelling sculptural object in its own right.
The complete Hanukkah lamp combines a shaped relief backplate with its projecting oil lights, making ritual function readable as metalwork.
The monumental Ilkhanid ewer combines a tall spout, faceted body, sphinxes and silver-inlaid inscription in an unusually clear, richly textured full object.
Animated calligraphy and inlaid metal ornament turn the Wade Cup’s simple bowl form into an exceptionally inventive Islamic sculptural surface.
The Edo royal commemorative head has a commanding face and elaborate cast crown; its ornament and bronze surface reward close inspection.
The Fang guardian head’s compact silhouette, polished dark surface and concentrated facial geometry make it a distinctive sculptural portrait.
Pettrich’s monumental reclining figure gives nineteenth-century American historical sculpture an emotionally direct, fully readable composition.
A long curved ivory horn tapers to a point beneath rows of relief carving; its sweeping outline reads clearly, with the small figures and patterns revealed on closer inspection.
